convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I stole from someone who trusted me. I think about it every day."
Rosa has an edge today — something curdled.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants. I mean it."
"My theory changes weekly. This week's: we're the control group. Somewhere there's a village that got instructions, and we're the ones they just... watched. Cheerful thought, right?"
"Still on what you think happened to us."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Walt is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Hah. We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 3 days back. 'They fill the quiet. Anyway — where was I?'"
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"Give it three more days of arguing. Then someone says the obvious thing and we all pretend it was theirs."
"Still on what's been happening."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Yeah? What's up? That's where we are."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You're one of the good ones. Don't make me regret saying that out loud." "That's where we are."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — still on my mind. I keep coming back to it."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know the old burn east of camp — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"The whole fire was arguing about Lockpick last night — what to even CALL it. 'Old Big' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we wandered off it, 7 days back. 'Yeah? What's up? That's where we are.'"
"My part? I clean up other people's messes quietly and stay ready."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Like I said — Still on what's been happening."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Don't laugh. Being buried somewhere unnamed."
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Honest. I can work with honest."
"Why do you ask? Mine's simple: learn one useful thing a week. This week it's carpentry. A plan's just a direction you argue with."
"What if it's not aliens? What if it's us — future us — running a simulation to figure out where we went wrong? We're homework."
"Take your time."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on the big questions. Good talking."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You know what — Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Me? New Orleans, Louisiana. I still dream in its weather — rain on a tin roof, that specific smell. I wake up here and for a second I'm furious at the sky for the swap. — ask anyone!"
"Still on where you're from."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Manreet owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Nobody says Manreet's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"I'm picking up Manreet's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What's something you're good at that nobody here knows about? I'm listening."
"Noted. Filing that under 'extremely useful.' The village needs that."
"I can do husbandry. Not well — well enough that nobody's died from it yet. That's my whole résumé now: nobody's died from it yet…"
"Still on what you're good at."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I know you and Manreet were close. I'm sorry."
"I keep turning over the last thing Manreet said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving. That's the whole of it."
"This one — Doum Palm. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Staghorn Sumac. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"Ha." Not amused. "I wasn't a barber. I was a lifeguard. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others. There. You happy?"
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Courtney rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Courtney shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Still on your read on people here. Makes sense to me."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We're down to 1 liters of clean water. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"1 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Loud-Eyes — It goes perfectly still. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"The 3x3 scan-mark burns into the ground. That's The Static Kite telling you it's about to move. Give it room. That's the whole lesson."
"Have you heard what they're calling The Paparazzo? Courtney is pushing 'Big-Bane'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
